Synopsis:
A sovereign myconid we call the brooding sovereign has been displaced to this myconid circle, after the duergar attackes his home. He would like to join you as you cleanse the area of duergar as a means of getting revenge - supposedly.

 The top block: The borroding myconid is with the other myconids. You can recruit it.

The middle block: You have killed the lone duergar. the myconid now wants you to kill all the duergars.

 Next block: you have killed all the duergars; now it wants you to kill the sovereign
. 
Final block: you have killed the sovereign and it rewards you. 

This myconid does not speak with the same hive mind voice of the others. He should sound creepy, like FART in Rick and Morty, with a SLIGHT undercurrent of menace.

 As the quest moves on, he gets more and more creepy and angry,

Cluster Contexts:

Early in the scene he can be recruited into your group, but as the quest progresses he pushes you from killing a lone duergar to clearing all the duergar, and finally to assassinating the rival Sovereign (Spaw) so only Glut remains. Some branches imply the player has already slain kin or other threats, which feeds Glut’s talk of “excising” a tumour and his hunger for dominance. He speaks apart from the other myconids in a creepy, sing-song voice with a low menace (think FART from Rick and Morty), and his tone steadily grows angrier and more threatening as he pressures the player to carry out bloodier acts.

context: Sovereign Glut is a displaced myconid sovereign who fled into this circle after duergar razed his home and now offers to join the player to “cleanse” the grotto—initially as revenge but increasingly as a bid for dominance. Early in the scene Glut can be recruited into the party, but the quest escalates: first to killing a lone duergar, then to wiping out all the duergar, and finally to assassinating the rival sovereign, Spaw, so Glut alone rules the circle. The rest of the myconids speak as a telepathic hive-mind (visions and music), but Glut speaks apart in a creepy, sing-song voice with a low, growing menace; his tone hardens as the player commits bloodier acts. Some branches imply the player has already slain kin or other threats, which Glut frames as “excising a tumour” and uses to justify increasingly violent demands.
